q: why did it jump in september?
answer:
Short answer: September didn’t show a clear jump in CAC for new customers — ad spend and new-customer counts both fell by ~46%, so CAC stayed roughly level once those moves are accounted for. The data points to matched declines in investment and volume, not a single failing channel.

What changed, and why it matters
- Ad spend fell from ₹22,03,894 (Aug) to ₹11,93,322 (Sep) (−45.9%) while new customers fell from 1,278 to 687 (−46.2%). Because spend and new-customer volume fell almost the same amount, their effects largely offset and CAC did not move strongly in one direction.
- By platform: Meta spend dropped ₹15,77,922 → ₹8,55,043 and new customers 833 → 439; Google spend dropped ₹6,25,972 → ₹3,38,279 and new customers 372 → 193. Both platforms contributed similar proportional declines.
- Secondary signals: gross and net sales also fell ~44–46%, contribution margin declined less (-36.6%) and Net ROAS improved slightly — the funnel compressed but efficiency per rupee was not the main issue.

Worth checking:
- Which campaigns had the biggest absolute drop in new-customer volume (not just share) — that will show where to restore spend first.

Period: 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 vs 2026-08-01..2026-08-31 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-28
